transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 16:00 PT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marcus Bell (Broadstone Head of ML), Sofia Ruiz (Infra Lead), Derek Kim (CTO)

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Alex with Redwood, and with me is Priya on the technical side. How are you all doing?
00:07 Marcus Bell: Doing good thanks, Marcus here. Yeah excited to learn more about Dedicated capacity; we're trying to lock down options for our inference platform.
00:13 Derek Kim: Hey all, Derek. Quick context from our side: we run multiple customer-facing models, some real-time chat assistants and rerankers, and we're getting hit on both cost and tail latency.
00:23 Priya Rao: Great thanks Marcus, Derek. Could you share current scale and SLOs? rough qps, p95, model sizes?
00:30 Marcus Bell: Sure, so right now we're doing about 800 to 1k qps across endpoints during peak, roughly 40% is chat gen at 2k token prompts, 30% embeddings, the rest are reranks and smaller prompts. Our p95 needs to be under 300ms for routing layer - but for the chat product we can tolerate up to 800-1,000ms depending on model.
00:49 Alex Chen: Cool, and what's your current hosting? cloud GPUs or managed APIs?
00:53 Marcus Bell: Mixed - we have some on-prem GPUs for sensitive data, and we use a mix of public cloud instances for burst. We're evaluating whether Dedicated reserved pools from Redwood can replace some public cloud capacity and give us more predictable costs and isolation.
01:04 Priya Rao: That's exactly where Dedicated fits - reserved GPU pools with customer isolation, can be in a VPC or private deployment. Quick question on models: are you using open weights, or vendor-hosted models?
01:12 Marcus Bell: Mostly open weights - tuned LLaMA derivatives, a couple of fine-tuned rerank models. We're also testing Claude style models for some safety layers.
01:19 Derek Kim: For us security is big - SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs. We need encryption keys in our KMS and strict egress control.
01:26 Alex Chen: Understood. We support VPC Dedicated with customer-managed KMS and audit logging. For Private deployments we can run in customer cloud or on-prem for full isolation.
01:34 Sofia Ruiz: A couple questions on burst handling - our traffic is spiky and we can't afford large cold starts. How do you handle burst capacity and autoscaling in Dedicated?
01:41 Priya Rao: Right, so Dedicated has two levers: reserved baseline capacity for predictable throughput, and a configurable burst pool you can opt into. The burst pool can be either Redwood-managed spare capacity or reserved warm nodes you pay a lower standby fee for to avoid cold starts. We also do intelligent routing and model-fanout to fallback to smaller quantized variants if the primary model is saturated.
02:01 Marcus Bell: What's the typical latency hit when you fallback to quantized models? like 8-bit or 4-bit variants?
02:07 Priya Rao: Usually 10-25% faster CPU/GPU throughput and minimal quality delta for many workloads, but it depends on prompt length and model. We'll need to benchmark your prompts.
02:15 Derek Kim: How does autoscaling trigger? is it reactive or predictive? we want to avoid cascading latency at scale.
02:21 Priya Rao: Autoscaling is policy-driven: you can set SLO targets, queue thresholds, and burst caps. There's also a pre-warming option based on scheduled patterns or recent traffic signals - so you can have warm standby replicas for predictable diurnal spikes.
02:33 Sofia Ruiz: For network isolation: if we go Dedicated in our VPC, do you require any outbound egress? we want zero egress to the public internet for some regulated workloads.
02:42 Alex Chen: For VPC Dedicated, control plane calls can be tunneled through customer-managed endpoints; in Private deployments we can run the entire control plane inside your network. We have customers with zero-public-egress setups. We'll need your network team to share firewall rules; Priya can follow up on specifics.
02:55 Marcus Bell: Cost question - how do you price baseline reserved nodes vs burst standby? any example numbers?
03:00 Alex Chen: We'll send a dedicated pricing deck after the call, but high level: baseline committed capacity is a monthly reservation with discounted hourly rates; burst standby is a smaller monthly fee to keep warm nodes or you can pay purely on use for Redwood-managed burst at higher per-hour rates. We can model your current bill if you share trace samples.
03:14 Marcus Bell: Ok that helps, we definitely want to model cost/latency tradeoffs.
03:18 Derek Kim: Another compliance question: do you provide customer-visible audit logs and token-level request logs? our security team needs tamper-evident logs for requests and KMS key usage.
03:27 Priya Rao: Yes, we provide audit logs and per-request telemetry. For Dedicated and Private we support forwarding logs to your SIEM, and KMS usage is logged in your KMS. We'll share the SOC2 and technical security whitepaper.
03:39 Sofia Ruiz: On scaling - we expect to double qps in 6 months and maybe triple in 12. How easy is capacity expansion and what's lead time for adding more GPUs?
03:48 Alex Chen: For Redwood Dedicated, we can scale within the cluster capacity quickly (minutes to hours) if there's headroom; adding new physical capacity or reserved pools will depend on region and hardware availability - typically days to weeks for large expansions. We recommend an autoscaling strategy with baseline cushion and scheduled pre-warm for known growth.
04:03 Marcus Bell: For the benchmark, what do you need from us? traces, prompt sets, traffic distribution?
04:08 Priya Rao: Exactly: two weeks of production traces (anonymized), representative prompt sets for each workload, target SLOs, and model versions. We'll run throughput and p95/p99 latency tests against your prompts and proposed cluster config.
04:19 Derek Kim: Do you support model pinning and rollout policies? we need canary deploys and automatic fallback if a new model regresses.
04:26 Priya Rao: Yes, rollout controls are first-class: traffic splits, canaries, A/B rollouts, and automatic fallback to a previous pinned version or a smaller variant if latency or error rate spikes.
04:36 Marcus Bell: Any limitations around KV cache or long context windows on Dedicated? we use a 32k context for some customers.
04:43 Priya Rao: We support long-context models and manage KV cache across nodes; for 32k you might need a specific kernel and memory profile - we'll note that for benchmarking.
04:51 Sofia Ruiz: Who would be our primary Redwood contacts for onboarding and SLA questions?
04:55 Alex Chen: Alex is primary for the commercial side, Priya is technical touchpoint. For enterprise customers we also assign a solutions engineer and CSM during onboarding.
05:03 Marcus Bell: Great. Any immediate blockers from our side?
05:06 Derek Kim: We need to validate SOC2 docs and confirm zero-public-egress options. Also want to see pricing and a trial plan.
05:14 Alex Chen: Sounds good - we'll send the pricing deck and SOC2/security docs. Priya will draft a benchmark plan and request the traces. Can we tentatively schedule the deep-dive for week of Mar 16?
05:24 Marcus Bell: That works for us.
05:26 Sofia Ruiz: We'll aim to get the infra diagrams and compliance list to you by next Friday.
05:30 Alex Chen: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and action items.
05:35 Marcus Bell: Thanks, bye.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription glitches noted in original auto-transcript (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash", "SOC2" as "S O C two"). Speakers sometimes labeled generically; this cleaned export keeps speaker labels but retains natural speech hesitations.
